title: ABF3 v10 — ABF2 Titles Results (Web)
front: `ads_web_abf_3_v10_abf2_titles_only` (Web) · device-randomized, four arms at 25% each · restarted 2026-10-09 23:30 UTC (same restart as OTT).

Control = ABF2 human cue points. v4 = T1 equal-load pruner (`abf3_pruner_t1_equal_load_v4.py`). v6 = T2, equal load plus about +7% ad load on movies of 60–120 minutes (`abf3_pruner_t2_targeted_load_v6.py`). v5b = T3, ABF2-like cue counts placed where the OTT ad config accepts requests (`abf3_pruner_t3_abf2_density_v5b.py`). The served cue lists are catalog-level, so every platform serves the same lists as OTT.

2026-10-09 → 2026-10-19 (complete days). Outcomes are capped at 2026-10-20 00:00 UTC; the exposures table is loaded through the end of 2026-10-19 (2026-10-20 is a partial day and is excluded). Same window as the refreshed OTT report. This is an early read of a live test, not a graduation read, and it has not been re-reconciled with a Statsig scorecard.

device-level CUPED, pre-period 2026-09-25 → 2026-10-08, Welch 95% intervals. ~6.99M devices/arm (ITT). Revenue is reported three ways — total (all billable ads), budgeted (direct, guaranteed, PMP), and unbudgeted (open auction, the v8 metric) — plus ad impressions and TVT. Same queries and definitions as the OTT report (Appendix C), run on the web experiment's exposures. Report date 2026-10-20.

Window extended from the end of 2026-10-18 to the end of 2026-10-19 (every complete day loaded in the exposures table); ITT devices/arm 6.28M → 6.99M. **Title set corrected:** the on-title, ToT, band, type and below-control tables now use the 224,739 targeted titles (`ml_dev.tmp.abf3_v10_targeted_titles`, the titles served v10 cue points) instead of the 299k live ABF2 catalog, which included about 74.5k titles that carry identical cues in every arm and so diluted every on-title and band lift. On-title ITT unbudgeted revenue, previous version → now (title set and window both changed): v4 −1.245% → −2.012%; v5b +3.653% → +4.123%; v6 +0.090% → +0.601%. Global ITT total revenue, previous version → now: v4 −1.529% → −1.635%; v5b +1.921% → +1.853%; v6 −0.280% → −0.329%. TVT: v4 −0.071% → −0.143%; v5b +0.179% → +0.248%; v6 +0.012% → +0.049%. No global ITT significance call changed. All tables, the band/type/below-control cuts, the gate replay and the viewing-depth numbers below were re-run.
tldr: v5b is the clear winner on web.
Total revenue +1.853% sig, budgeted +1.845% sig, unbudgeted +2.298% sig, impressions +1.991% sig. On the targeted titles open-auction revenue is +4.123% sig. TVT flat (+0.248% ns).
Total revenue v4 −1.635% sig (budgeted −1.598% sig), v6 −0.329% ns. Neither moves TVT.
Episodes split the arms, as on mobile.
Episode open-auction revenue: v5b +4.72% sig, v6 −4.04% sig, v4 −4.00% sig. Movies: v6 +5.92% sig, v5b +2.40% sig, v4 +2.13% ns.
Web is a small, noisy surface.

Only ~9% of exposed web devices watched anything in-window (Active n ≈ 652K/arm), and total revenue is ~$0.02 per exposed device in the window. Intervals are wide; at the headline level only v5b's gain and v4's loss clear zero.
No TVT move is significant in any population, band, type, or below-control cut.
tldr_note: All figures are global ITT CUPED lifts versus Control. Direction is stable across ITT, Active, and ToT (v4's total-revenue loss is also significant in Active and ToT). Significance calls are nominal 95% (not adjusted for sequential looks or three arms) and the interval widening seen on the Statsig scorecard (~1.8× on the 10-15 OTT read) would apply here too; not re-checked against Statsig for this window.
headline_intro: All figures are CUPED lifts versus Control, 95% intervals. Global is across every title an exposed device watched. On-title is the same devices, restricted to the 224,739 targeted titles — the ABF2-catalog titles served v10 cue points. ToT is defined on the same set. “Sig” means the interval excludes zero (nominal p < 0.05).
money_read: v5b gains in every pool, with the largest lift in the open auction (+2.298% sig) — the opposite of OTT, where v5b's gain comes mostly through budgeted demand. v4's loss is in the budgeted pool (−1.598% sig); its open-auction revenue is −1.042% ns.
ontitle_read: On the targeted titles v5b is +4.123% sig (ITT), +2.524% sig (Active), +2.477% sig (ToT). v4 is −2.012% sig (ITT), −2.569% sig (Active), −2.626% sig (ToT) — significantly negative on the treated titles even though its global unbudgeted revenue is −1.042% ns; v6 is +0.601% ns (ITT), not significant. On-title TVT is flat for all arms.
npv_read: No TVT move is significant for either viewer type. Power viewers are rare on web (~0.23%), so that row is very wide.
band_read: v5b gains in the sparse bands: 1–3 +8.57% sig, 4–6 +7.18% sig. v4 and v6 lose at 1–3 (−6.04% sig, −8.45% sig).
10–12 is the positive pocket for every arm: v6 +6.67% sig, v5b +3.94% sig, v4 +3.59% sig.
7–9 and 13+ are not significant for any arm. Band cells on web are small (81–251K devices), so only large moves clear zero.
TVT is flat in every band.
below_read: Same direction as OTT and mobile for v4 and v6: below-control titles lose and at/above-control titles gain. Significant cells: v4 10–12 below −9.04% sig; v4 10–12 at/above +8.47% sig; v4 13+ below −3.51% sig; v5b 10–12 at/above +4.83% sig; v5b 13+ below −3.05% sig; v6 10–12 below −8.39% sig; v6 10–12 at/above +8.35% sig; v6 13+ below −3.74% sig; v6 13+ at/above +5.92% sig. Cells not listed are not significant at web sample sizes. The per-title floor case holds on web.
type_read: Episodes split the arms: v5b +4.72% sig, v6 −4.04% sig, v4 −4.00% sig. Movies: v6 +5.92% sig, v5b +2.40% sig, v4 +2.13% ns. TVT flat.
gate_intro: Replay the pod gate (greedy first-eligible) over the ABF2 and served positions, weighted by each title's in-window web TVT. The web ad config is not in the project files, so two gate profiles are shown: A = OTT base gates, and B = the most tolerant OTT ladder step. Observed web midrolls start earlier than OTT (median first episode break ~491s vs ~652s on OTT, measured on a 2026-10-12/13 sample), so B is the closer approximation. Profile B fits the measured per-band impression lifts clearly better (r = 0.49 vs 0.31 across the 15 arm×band cells).
gate_read: Under the tolerant profile v5b fires more episode breaks in every band (+4.5% to +20.8%) and v4/v6 fire fewer from 4–6 up (v4 −1.2% at 4–6 to −4.6% at 13+) — the measured episode split. Web episode viewing is shallower than OTT (81.2% of ABF2 episode views reach ~6.3 min, 78.6% reach ~9.7 min; OTT 91.4% / 89.7%), which likely adds to v4/v6's late-first-cue penalty on sparse episodes.
decomp_read: For v4/v6 the episode losses come mostly from fewer cue points under both profiles → the per-title floor is the lever. For v5b the tolerant profile makes the count term positive: ABF2-density lists fire more breaks when gates are looser.
decision_intro: Early read, same window as OTT. Web is the smallest and noisiest surface; treat everything except v5b's gain and v4's loss as directional.
decision: Total revenue +1.853% sig, open-auction +2.298% sig, on-title +4.123% sig, TVT flat. It is the only arm with a significant total-revenue gain on all three platforms (on mobile with a small TVT dip).
v4 should not ship to web.
Total revenue −1.635% sig, driven by budgeted demand (−1.598% sig).
Total revenue −0.329% ns; its movie gain (+5.92% sig) is offset by the episode loss (−4.04% sig).
Get the web ad config to replace the approximate gate profiles; a longer window is needed for the band and below-control cells.
pool_read: For v5b both pools rise (budgeted +1.973% sig, unbudgeted +2.596% sig): new inventory filled by both demand types, a clean incrementality signal. v4's budgeted impressions fall (−1.601% sig).
methods: One variant per device from `core_dev.statsig.exposures` for `ads_web_abf_3_v10_abf2_titles_only`; no device has more than one variant. Outcomes require event time at/after first exposure.

Outcomes 2026-10-09 through 2026-10-19, capped at 2026-10-20 00:00 UTC. CUPED covariate 2026-09-25 → 2026-10-08. Active = ≥1 video session since first exposure in-window. ToT = ≥1 second of TVT on a targeted title (the 224,739 titles in `ml_dev.tmp.abf3_v10_targeted_titles`) in-window.

Identical to the OTT report. On-title, ToT, band, type and below-control tables use the 224,739 targeted titles (`ml_dev.tmp.abf3_v10_targeted_titles`: ABF2-catalog titles — movie/episode streams with non-empty `cue_points_abf`, excluding `abf3_pruned_v8` and the v8 title table — that were served v10 cue points); the other ~74.5k catalog titles carry identical cues in every arm and are excluded (versions before 2026-10-20 included them and understated on-title and band lifts); total / budgeted / unbudgeted revenue from `core_prod.ads.impressions` × `mercurydb_cdc.campaigns` with the v8 advertiser exclusions; device-level CUPED with pooled theta per population, Welch 95% (z = 1.96). Band/type/below-control tables are raw Welch.

Same simulation as OTT, re-run as a SQL port of `v10_gate_replay.py` (`gate_replay_all.sql`; validated against the 10-15 notebook run), TVT weights from in-window video sessions on this platform. Gate values are approximations — see §2c.

`ml_dev.tmp.abf3_new_pruner_cuepoints` (snapshot 2026-10-08; T1 = v4, T2 = v6, T3 = v5b; the table now also holds extra arms that are not part of v10 and were excluded) — catalog-level, so §B.4 and the first-cue table match the OTT report.
Queries and scripts in `abf-experiment/v10_verification/` (refresh outputs in `results_20261020/`).
